title: Find a graph minimum
intro: Use the minimum to choose when a pump starts and calculate its least energy use.

beats.spoken: On a Graphs page, enter the function you want to investigate and press Enter.
beats.coach: A greenhouse can start its pump x hours after sunrise (0 ≤ x ≤ 6). The model gives daily energy E = x² − 6x + 13 kWh. When should it start, and what is the least energy use?

beats.spoken: Open Menu, choose Analyze Graph, and select Minimum.
beats.coach: The question asks for the lowest output, not where E is zero. Open Menu → 6: Analyze Graph → 2: Minimum.

beats.spoken: We're looking for the lowest point in the interval you choose.
beats.coach: The pump can start from 0 to 6 hours after sunrise. Choose narrower search bounds around the valley, not the entire allowed time by default.

beats.spoken: To set the lower bound, move the cursor to the left of the minimum, then press Enter.
beats.coach: Place the lower bound to the left of the valley and press Enter. You are bracketing a visible turning point, not estimating its coordinate yet.

beats.spoken: For the upper bound, move to the right of the minimum and press Enter again.
beats.coach: Place the upper bound to the right of the same valley and press Enter. The shaded band should enclose just that valley.
There is one valley in the band. The curve opens upward and the valley lies inside the allowed interval, so neither endpoint can give a lower energy use.

beats.spoken: The calculator marks the minimum and shows its coordinates.
beats.coach: Read the two coordinates beside the marker: (3, 4). They describe the best start time and the energy use at that time.

beats.spoken: The x-coordinate tells you where it occurs.
beats.coach: The first coordinate is a time: start the pump 3 hours after sunrise.

beats.spoken: The y-coordinate is the minimum value.
beats.coach: The second coordinate is the least energy use: 4 kWh. Enter again only if you want to pin the coordinate label.
